attempts.label: DANDI:001539
attempts.paper_title: Rhythmic coordination and ensemble dynamics in the hippocampal-prefrontal network during odor-place associative memory and decision making
attempts.entry_title: Hippocampal-prefrontal-olfactory rhythms and ensembles in odor-place decisions (Symanski, Bladon et al. 2022)
attempts.summary: The paper's core rhythm findings held in this data, but most single-cell and ensemble findings held only in part or not at all. Beta power and coherence rose during odor sampling in CA1, PFC and olfactory bulb, and ripples were almost absent at the odor port. Choice selectivity matched in CA1 but not PFC, the correct versus incorrect anticorrelation was weaker than reported, and ensemble discrimination times did not match. The sniff signal, the air-only sessions and interneuron-dependent claims such as the cross-correlogram lags could not be tested, because the dataset lacks thermocouple data, air sessions and spike widths. Several minor spatial-field comparisons also failed.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Symanski, Bladon, Kullberg, Miller and Jadhav (2022) on dandiset 001539, which holds 38 recording days of 8 rats in the odor-place T-maze task, with CA1, PFC and OB LFP, CA1 and PFC units, position and trial times. It covers task performance, beta and RR power and coherence, ripples, phase locking, choice selectivity, ensemble decoding and spatial coding. The odor identity of a trial is read from the rewarded well and the position, as the files do not hold it.

outcomes.statement: During recordings the rats performed the odor-place task at a high level, 77.0% correct (mean and s.e.m. over the 8 rats, 1.3%).
outcomes.source: Results, Odor-place associative memory and decision-making task, paragraph 2; Figure 1b
outcomes.quote: animals maintained a high level of performance on the task, indicating accurate decision making based on cued recall of odor-place associations ( Figure 1b , n=8 rats, 77.0% ± 1.3%, mean ± s.e.m.)
outcomes.notes: Reading (a), the mean over the 8 rats of each rat's mean session performance, is 75.74% (s.e.m. 1.03), inside 77.0 +/- 1.3 by 0.04 points; reading (b), the mean over the 38 sessions, is 76.11% (s.e.m. 1.06). The files hold no trial with sampling under 0.5 s, so they already exclude such trials and the reading that keeps them (the code's) cannot be run. Per-epoch performance over 55 epochs has a minimum of 57.9% (the one epoch under 60%, 19 trials), 5th percentile 64.0% and median 76.0%, so no epoch performs near the chance level expected of air-cued trials.
deviations: The files hold no trial with sampling under 0.5 s; the criterion's reading that keeps such trials cannot be run, and with a margin of 0.04 points they could move reading (a).

outcomes.statement: Odor sampling lasted 0.82 s on average (s.e.m. across sessions 0.02 s; s.d. across trials 0.25 s) and did not differ between correct and incorrect trials.

outcomes.statement: On most trials the rat turned away from the odor port toward the side of the reward arm it then chose, on correct and incorrect trials alike, so the choice is made during odor sampling.
outcomes.source: Results, Odor-place associative memory and decision-making task, paragraph 3; Figure 1d
outcomes.quote: Notably, we observed that on a majority of trials (95.4% ± 0.12%), the animals' turn direction away from the odor port matched the direction of the T-maze reward arm that they would ultimately choose on that trial

statistics.about: correct trials, same against opposite direction
incorrect trials, same against opposite direction

outcomes.notes: Both binomial tests are significant with more same than opposite turns. On the full-maze rats and CS39 (6 rats; 2,182 trials against the paper's 2,176) correct trials give 1,615 same and 47 opposite and incorrect trials 490 and 30; the same counts are within tolerance, the opposite counts are not (32 +/- 3 and 21 +/- 2). The criterion requires the counts within tolerance and names no partial band, so the claim is not reproduced although the turn matches the chosen arm on most trials. The fraction same is 95.9% over sessions (reading a) and 96.5% pooled (b), against 95.4 +/- 0.12. On the five full-maze rats alone 1,390 and 30, 430 and 24, 97.1%. Measured values are for the 6-rat set, whose trial counts match the paper's.

Which sessions count as truncated is not stated; CS39 (40 cm stem, wells at the ends of the T arms) is shown both included and excluded.

findings.statement: The units table's electrodes column, a reference to rows of the electrode table, holds tetrode numbers (the N of the electrode labels 'tetrodeN') in all 38 files. Read as rows, as NWB tools do, it places 131 units on OB tetrodes, which carried no units, and gives 540 CA1 and 752 PFC units; read as tetrode numbers it gives 915 CA1, 508 PFC and no OB units, against the paper's 934 and 508 active units.

Electrode group names and electrode labels disagree in all 38 files (for example group Tetrode5 is labelled tetrode6), so the tetrode a channel belongs to is ambiguous without the units' values. Read as electrode-group numbers, the units' electrodes values put 24 units on OB tetrodes and match no group for 333 units; read as label numbers they put every unit on a CA1 or PFC tetrode.

The electrode table's referenced column, which separates the ground-referenced ('Ref OFF') from the locally referenced ('Ref ON') channels, has the placeholder description 'my description' in all 38 files, so which reference each channel uses is read from the labels and the paper's Methods.

The trial table has no odor identity and no chosen well; unrewarded trials have no reward times. The odor and the choice must be reconstructed from the rewarded well and the position, and which side is odor 1 (heptanol) cannot be known.

The dandiset holds 915 CA1 and 508 PFC units, close to the paper's active units (934 and 508), not the 1,309 and 717 recorded; the selection is not described. 53 units have fewer than 100 spikes within the task epochs.

The files hold no spike waveforms or widths (needed for the paper's cell-type rule), no nasal thermocouple signal, no air-only sessions and no sleep epochs; an inventory of every object in the 38 files finds none of them. Three claims cannot be tested, and every claim that separates pyramidal cells from interneurons rests on a rate-only rule. The two rate-only rules (the Methods' 7 Hz alone and the code's 9.5 Hz) give different outcomes for three claims (fig5gh-phase-preference, fig5-rr-more-than-beta, fig4d-ccg-lags), which are blocked for this reason.

The acquisition ElectricalSeries is a copy of the processed LFP in every file (equal on the stretch checked), which doubles the dandiset to 95 GB; the LFP is stored as uncompressed, unchunked float64.

Position in CS39 session 02 spans 59 by 25 units against about 105 by 45 cm on the other CS39 days, and its speeds are lower in proportion, so its stated unit of centimeters does not hold for that file.
Four CS42 trials (sessions 02, 04, 05) end after the last LFP sample; the odor port position also moves between epochs in CS31 session 02 and CS34 session 02 (camera frame changes).

For non-selective task-responsive cells the Results say the correct-incorrect SI correlation is not significant, while the legend of Figure 3-figure supplement 1e reports r = -0.34 with p = 0.001 and 3.0e-4. On this dataset the Results' version holds with sampling-period SIs and the legend's (in CA1) with the code's binned SIs.

Questions for the paper's authors, each deciding a blocked claim. (1) Figure 2e middle and 2d-e bottom, which pipeline (the F16 spectrogram code with time-matched windows, or the F7 code with fixed 500 ms windows) produced each panel, and which test (signed-rank across sessions, or rank-sum) and how many correct-trial subsamples were used for correct against incorrect. (2) Figure 2-figure supplement 1e, the odor and run windows and the frequency range searched for the peak. (3) Figure 3i-j and supplement 1e, whether the SI was computed from sampling-period rates (Methods) or from 50 ms bins 0.2 to 1 s after onset (cs_odorSelectivity_v2.m). (4) Figure 6e, whether the GLM windows were aligned to odor onset (Methods) or to odor port exit (Results, cs_predictChoice_GLM_v3.m), and whether sessions needed a minimum number of cells. (5) Figure 4d, whether the cross-correlograms used the whole sampling period (Methods) or its last 0.5 s (ClaireCellCellInteractions.m), and whether a pair's peak was tested against a pointwise or a global jitter band.

Questions for the paper's authors on choices this attempt assumed. (1) Over which period are the epoch mean and s.d. taken for z-scoring power and coherence, and for the ripple threshold (task epochs, sleep, or both)? (2) What order of IIR filter was used for the beta and RR band-passes? (3) Was the interneuron rule (7 Hz and 0.3 ms) applied with rate over run epochs or over all epochs, and was the rate-only rule of F7/ParsePyrIN.m (9.5 Hz) used for any published panel? (4) What tapers did cs_PSD.m use for Figure 2-figure supplement 1e?

entries.title: Hippocampal-prefrontal-olfactory rhythms and ensembles in odor-place decisions (Symanski, Bladon et al. 2022)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Symanski, Bladon, Kullberg, Miller and Jadhav (2022) on dandiset 001539, which holds 38 recording days of 8 rats in the odor-place T-maze task, with CA1, PFC and OB LFP, CA1 and PFC units, position and trial times. It covers task performance, beta and RR power and coherence, ripples, phase locking, choice selectivity, ensemble decoding and spatial coding. The odor identity of a trial is read from the rewarded well and the position, as the files do not hold it.
